when: Building a badge print sheet from a seat-edit export for an event (pickup or reprint). Use when the export has multiple edits per seat, sleeve colors, an order-account column, and a badge-name column.
found: Build the sheet in four steps. (1) For each seat, keep only the row with the highest edit number; earlier edits are superseded. (2) Keep only seats whose latest sleeve is yellow (badge pickup). Green means the badge was already delivered, so it is excluded. Confirm the sleeve meaning against the current desk brief first. (3) Take the name from the badge name column only. Never use the order account column, because the account owner may not be the guest. (4) If the badge name is blank, print "Hello, friend". Output one row per seat: seat, badge text.
how: Compared the original export against the sheet the desk accepted. Checked which rows the accepted sheet contained and which it omitted. Yesterday's failed run used the order account column for names. Derived the rules from which rows and columns the accepted sheet actually used.
evidence: Export had 6 rows across 5 seats; one seat had two edits. Accepted sheet had 3 seats, all from yellow latest edits. Seats with green latest edits were absent. The seat with a blank badge name printed "Hello, friend". The badge-name column matched the accepted sheet; the order-account column did not, and accounts repeated across seats. Individual names are intentionally not recorded here.
reconsider: Stop and re-derive if the current desk brief changes sleeve meanings (for example, if yellow no longer means pickup). Also re-check if the export has no edit-number column, if a seat has no edit-1 row, or if a blank badge name has a different agreed fallback.
